title: Forward Converter (isolated)
summary: Galvanically isolated buck-derived converter; a transformer delivers energy during the on-time into an LC output filter, giving the CCM ratio n * D, where n = N2/N1 is the turns ratio. Unlike the flyback it has no right-half-plane zero.

ports.name: in
ports.description: Positive primary-side input supply rail feeding the primary winding and switch.

ports.name: sw
ports.description: Primary switching node between the primary winding and the low-side switch.

ports.name: out
ports.description: Isolated regulated output rail across the LC filter and load (secondary side).

ports.name: pri_gnd
ports.description: Primary-side ground reference (input return); also returns the reset/tertiary winding.

ports.name: sec_gnd
ports.description: Secondary-side ground reference (output return), galvanically isolated from pri_gnd.

ports.name: pwm
ports.description: Gate-drive command for the primary switch from the controller.

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Steady-state duty cycle of the primary switch.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Power transformer turns ratio n = N2/N1 (secondary over primary).

parameters.name: n31
parameters.description: Reset (tertiary) winding turns ratio n31 = N3/N1; sets the demagnetization interval and the switch voltage stress.

parameters.name: LM
parameters.description: Primary magnetizing inductance (governs the magnetizing/reset current; ideally large enough to be negligible in the power path).

parameters.name: R_load
parameters.description: Load resistance seen at the output (R_load = Vout / Iout).

parameters.name: r_L
parameters.description: Output inductor series resistance (DCR); dominant loss term affecting the DC conversion ratio.

parameters.name: r_C
parameters.description: Output capacitor equivalent series resistance (ESR); sets the high-frequency zero.

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio
design_equations.description: Ideal CCM DC conversion ratio (Alonso eq. 5.18 lossless); the buck ratio D scaled by the turns ratio n.

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio_with_losses
design_equations.expression: Vout / Vin = n * D / (1 + r_L / R_load)
design_equations.description: CCM DC conversion ratio including the output inductor series resistance r_L (Alonso eq. 5.19); the capacitor ESR does not affect the DC ratio because no DC current flows in C.

design_equations.name: demagnetization_constraint
design_equations.expression: dt_reset = n31 * D / fsw < (1 - D) / fsw  =>  D_max < 1 / (1 + n31),  n31 = N3/N1
design_equations.description: The transformer must fully reset each cycle (Alonso eq. 5.3-5.6): the demagnetization interval n31*D*T must finish before the period ends. With an equal-turns reset winding (n31 = 1) the duty cycle is limited to D < 0.5.

design_equations.name: inductor_current
design_equations.description: Average output inductor current equals the load current in CCM (the LC filter keeps the output current continuous, as in a buck).

design_equations.name: inductor_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output inductor current ripple in CCM (Alonso eq. 5.42); the buck ripple with the reflected input n*Vin.

design_equations.name: rectifier_peak_current
design_equations.description: Peak current through the secondary rectifiers D1/D2 and the output inductor in CCM (Alonso summary).

design_equations.name: switch_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak blocking voltage across the primary switch (Alonso summary); set by the reset winding ratio. With n31 = 1 the switch must block 2*Vin, plus any leakage spike.

design_equations.name: reset_diode_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak reverse voltage across the reset (tertiary) diode D3 (Alonso summary).

design_equations.name: output_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in CCM for an ideal capacitor (Alonso eq. 5.43); ESR adds r_C * dI_L on top. Triangular inductor current into C gives the 1/8 factor, exactly as in the buck.

design_equations.name: boundary_load_resistance
design_equations.description: CCM-DCM boundary load resistance (Alonso eq. 5.45): CCM when R_load < R_lim, DCM when R_load > R_lim (same as the buck).

design_equations.name: boundary_output_current
design_equations.description: Output current at the CCM-DCM boundary (Alonso eq. 5.44).

design_equations.name: dcm_conversion_ratio
design_equations.expression: Vout / Vin = 2 * n / (1 + sqrt(1 + 4 * k / D**2)),  k = 2 * L * fsw / R_load
design_equations.description: DCM DC conversion ratio (Alonso eq. 5.55-5.56); the buck DCM ratio multiplied by the turns ratio n, load-dependent.

design_equations.name: dcm_output_ripple
design_equations.expression: dVout = L * ((n * Vin - Vout) * D / (L * fsw) - Vout / R_load)**2 / (2 * C * (1 - Vout / (n * Vin)) * Vout)
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in DCM (Alonso eq. 5.57); the buck DCM ripple with the reflected input n*Vin.

design_equations.name: ccm_characteristic_polynomial
design_equations.expression: Den(s) = L*C*(1 + r_C/R_load)*s**2 + (L/R_load + r_C*C + r_L*C + r_L*r_C*C/R_load)*s + (1 + r_L/R_load)
design_equations.description: Shared CCM denominator of every small-signal transfer function below; identical to the buck (a complex pole pair near 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C))), because the forward is dynamically a buck seen through the transformer.

design_equations.name: control_to_output_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Control-to-output transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 5.31-5.32); the buck Gd(s) multiplied by the turns ratio n (n*Vin = Vout/D). Single ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C), no right-half-plane zero.

design_equations.name: audio_susceptibility_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Input-to-output (audio susceptibility) transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 5.33); the buck Gb(s) multiplied by n, same dynamics as Gd(s).

design_equations.name: output_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop output impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 5.39); identical to the buck and independent of the turns ratio (the secondary side is a plain LC filter). Zo(0) approx r_L, Zo(inf) approx r_C.

design_equations.name: input_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop input impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 5.35); the buck input impedance divided by the turns ratio squared, with Zi(0) = (R_load + r_L)/(n**2*D**2) and Zi(inf) -> infinity.

control_notes: The forward converter is dynamically a buck converter seen through the power transformer: the secondary feeds a continuous-current LC output filter, so the control-to-output plant Gd(s) is a second-order low-pass with a complex LC pole pair and a single ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C) - and crucially NO right-half-plane zero (the key advantage over the flyback). Voltage-mode control with a Type-II/Type-III compensator is straightforward; cross over well below fsw/5, or use current-mode to drop the plant to first order. Every CCM transfer function is the buck result scaled by the turns ratio: Gd and Gb are n times the buck, the output impedance Zo is identical (independent of n), and the input impedance Zi is the buck value divided by n**2. In DCM (R_load > R_lim = 2*L*fsw/(1-D)) the plant collapses to first order and the DC gain becomes load-dependent (still n times the buck). The distinctive design constraint is transformer reset: the magnetizing flux must return to zero each cycle through a reset/tertiary winding (ratio n31 = N3/N1), an RCD clamp, or an active clamp. The reset interval n31*D*T must finish before the period ends, which limits the duty cycle to D_max < 1/(1 + n31) (D < 0.5 for an equal-turns reset winding) and sets the switch blocking voltage to (1 + 1/n31)*Vin plus any leakage-inductance spike. Feedback must cross the isolation barrier (optocoupler + shunt reference, or primary-side regulation). All small-signal results follow from the averaged dependent-source model: the switch is replaced by its average current source and the diodes by their average voltage sources, then linearized about the DC operating point.

reference.source: J. Marcos Alonso, Modelling, Control and Simulation of DC-DC Converters
